bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar's GI-Tagged Mithila Makhana Expands Global Reach, Exports Cross 7000 Tonnes
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar’s GI-Tagged Mithila Makhana Expands Global Reach, Exports Cross 7,000 Tonnes IBEF October 21, 2026 India exported more than 7,000 metric tonnes of makhana and value-added makhana products to over 20 international markets in FY26, according to the Ministry of Commerce. These markets include the United States, the Middle East and Africa, reflecting the product’s expanding global reach. Bihar accounts for nearly 85% of India’s makhana production, making it the country’s leading producer. Mithila Makhana, which has a Geographical Indication (GI) tag, is gaining international recognition for its nutritional benefits and versatility. Growing health awareness, startups developing value-added products and the participation of Farmer-Producer Organisations (FPOs) are helping expand the sector beyond its traditional markets. India is the world’s largest producer of makhana, with cultivation concentrated mainly in Bihar, West Bengal and Assam. The Government of India has introduced measures to strengthen the sector and support exports. A separate Harmonised System (HS) code for makhana came into effect in July 2025, enabling its distinct classification in international trade. The National Makhana Board, announced in the Union Budget 2025-26, was formally launched in Bihar on September 15, 2025. In addition, the government approved the Central Sector Scheme for the Development of Makhana, with an outlay of Rs. 476.03 crore (US$ 53.87 million) for 2025-26 to 2030-31. The scheme focuses on research and innovation, quality seed availability, farmer training, improved harvesting and post-harvest practices, value addition, branding, marketing, exports and quality control. Allocations of Rs. 30 crore (US$ 3.39 million) for FY26 and Rs. 90 crore (US$ 9.47 million) for FY27 have been approved under the scheme. These initiatives aim to modernise makhana cultivation and processing, strengthen farmers’ incomes and expand the global market for Bihar’s GI-tagged Mithila Makhana. national_raw_news.title: Week-long International Kullu Dussehra to begin today in Himachal Pradesh
national_raw_news.content: The world-famous International Kullu Dussehra in Himachal Pradesh will begin today with the Rath Yatra of Lord Shri Raghunath Ji. The seven-day festival will continue until October 27. Governor Kavinder Gupta will participate in the Rath Yatra and formally inaugurate the festival in the evening at Lal Chand Prarthi Kala Kendra. Akashvani correspondent reports that preparations for the International Kullu Dussehra have been completed. Amid the sounds of traditional musical instruments, deities and their devotees continue to arrive in Kullu from different parts of the district. Goddess Hidimba, the presiding deity of Manali, has also arrived in Kullu. The Rath Yatra of Lord Shri Raghunath Ji will be taken out today, marking the beginning of the festivities and bringing together a large gathering of deities. This year, laser and drone shows will be special attractions during the seven-day festival. Cultural troupes from India and abroad will also present a variety of performances, showcasing traditional folk arts and cultural diversity. Security arrangements have been tightened for the festival. More than 1,200 police personnel have been deployed to maintain law and order and manage crowds. The International Kullu Dussehra is a major celebration of Himachal Pradesh’s rich Dev Sanskriti and folk traditions, attracting tourists from across India and abroad.

national_raw_news.title: World Iodine Deficiency Day: Causes, symptoms and prevention of iodine deficiency
national_raw_news.content: World Iodine Deficiency Day: Causes, symptoms and prevention of iodine deficiency - India Today India Today Aaj Tak India Today Hindi NewsTak GNTTV Lallantop Business Today Bangla Malayalam Northeast BT Bazaar Harper's Bazaar Sports Tak Astro Tak Gaming Brides Today Cosmopolitan Kisan Tak Reader’s Digest India Today Aaj Tak India Today Hindi NewsTak GNTTV Lallantop Business Today Bangla Malayalam Northeast SIGN IN Edition IN IN US Download App Follow Us On: News Health World Iodine Deficiency Day: Causes, symptoms and prevention of iodine deficiency World Iodine Deficiency Day: Causes, symptoms and prevention of iodine deficiency Iodine plays a vital role in thyroid hormone production, metabolism and brain development. Adequate iodine intake, particularly during pregnancy and childhood, can help prevent serious health complications. Advertisement World Iodine Deficiency Day 2026: How iodised salt helps prevent health problems By: India Today Health Desk New Delhi , Oct 21, 2026 11:19 IST Last Updated Oct 21, 2026 11:19 IST Published by Smarica Pant Oct 21, 2026 11:17 IST Iodine is an essential mineral that the body needs to produce thyroid hormones, which regulate metabolism, growth and development. Although the body needs only small amounts of iodine, insufficient intake can lead to several health problems, including thyroid disorders and impaired brain development. The risks are especially serious during pregnancy and early childhood, when the brain and nervous system develop rapidly. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story World Iodine Deficiency Day, also known as Global Iodine Deficiency Disorders Prevention Day, is observed on October 21 every year to raise awareness about the importance of iodine and the consequences of its deficiency. In India, the government has introduced several initiatives to promote iodised salt consumption and reduce iodine deficiency disorders. Here is what you need to know about iodine, its health benefits and the steps being taken to prevent deficiency. WHAT IS IODINE AND WHY DOES THE BODY NEED IT Iodine is a mineral required to produce the thyroid hormone's thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3). These hormones help regulate metabolism, body temperature, growth and energy use. Iodine is naturally present in certain foods, including seafood, dairy products and eggs. Iodised salt is another important source. The amount of iodine in food depends on factors such as soil conditions and food production methods. World Iodine Deficiency day (Picture credit: pib.gov.in) HEALTH RISKS OF IODINE DEFICIENCY Insufficient iodine intake can prevent the thyroid gland from producing enough hormones. This may lead to hypothyroidism, which can cause tiredness, weight gain and other symptoms. Goitre, or an enlarged thyroid gland, is another possible sign of iodine deficiency. During pregnancy, severe iodine deficiency can affect fetal growth and brain development and increase the risk of miscarriage and stillbirth. In infants and children, inadequate iodine can affect cognitive development and learning. Prolonged deficiency can also affect growth and overall health. INDIA'S EFFORTS TO PREVENT IODINE DEFICIENCY India launched the National Goitre Control Programme in 1962 to address iodine deficiency. In 1992, it was expanded and renamed the National Iodine Deficiency Disorders Control Programme...

national_raw_news.title: SBI data breach: PSU bank confirms 3,897 customer records exposed on dark web
national_raw_news.content: SBI data breach: PSU bank confirms 3,897 customer records exposed on dark web - Telangana Today NRI View Point cartoon My Space Reviews Education Today Property Lifestyle Home | Business | Sbi Data Breach Psu Bank Confirms 3897 Customer Records Exposed On Dark Web SBI data breach: PSU bank confirms 3,897 customer records exposed on dark web State Bank of India confirmed that 3,897 customer records containing personal information were identified during a preliminary analysis of data found on the dark web. The lender has launched an investigation and said the incident has not disrupted core business operations By IANS Published Date - 21 October 2026, 10:43 AM New Delhi: State Bank of India (SBI) — India’s largest lender — on Wednesday clarified that it experienced a data breach with 3,897 customer records found exposed on the dark web. According to the bank, it has received communications from its Threat Intelligence Service Provider, the Defence Cyber Agency and CERT-In regarding an alert concerning suspected exposure of customer data earlier in the week. During preliminary analysis of approximately 375,000 records available on the dark web, 3,897 customer records containing Personally Identifiable Information (PII) were identified, the bank said in an exchange filing. The exposed information reportedly included customers’ registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, names, gender, email addresses, residential addresses, branch and CIF identifiers, lead IDs and metadata associated with loan/lead records and other related files, it added. The state-owned bank further noted that it promptly activated its cyber incident response and containment protocols and engaged an independent CERT-In-empanelled cybersecurity agency to conduct a comprehensive assessment and investigate the nature and extent of the alleged compromise. The bank said a detailed investigation is underway to establish authenticity and completeness of the exposed data, determine potential source and extent of exposure and assess associated risks. The incident does not have any material impact on its core business operations, financial performance or business continuity and core functions continue to operate normally without disruption, the bank said adding that appropriate remedial and preventive measures are being implemented. Shares of SBI on Wednesday traded on a flat note at Rs 970 at around 10 am on the BSE. The banking stock recorded a 52-week high of Rs 1,234.80 and a 52-week low of Rs 891.55, according to the exchange data. In the last one-year horizon, it declined 12 per cent but gained over the last five years. Earlier in the week, an unidentified hacker group operating under the name ‘Siriusim’ claimed to have obtained confidential customer information allegedly linked to the State Bank of India (SBI), including personal details, loan applications and account-opening documents. The claim was highlighted by cybersecurity monitoring account CyberPulse56 in a post on social media platform X. The group purportedly possesses 3.75 lakh data entries in CSV format and 2,722 PDF documents associated with the country’s largest public sector lender, as per the post. national_raw_news.title: 'No Double Standards On Terrorism': At SCO Summit, Rajnath Singh Calls For Collective ...
national_raw_news.content: 'No Double Standards On Terrorism': At SCO Summit, Rajnath Singh Calls For Collective Action To Dismantle Terror Ecosystem Security 'No Double Standards On Terrorism': At SCO Summit, Rajnath Singh Calls For Collective Action To Dismantle Terror Ecosystem Swarajya Staff Oct 21, 2026 | Updated 08:53 AM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Sign In Prefer Prefer Defence Minister Rajnath Singh (Pic Via PIB) Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Tuesday (20 October) called upon Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) member states to work together to dismantle the entire ecosystem of terrorism, asserting that there could be no justification for the menace or double standards in dealing with it. Addressing the 25th meeting of the SCO Council of Heads of Government in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, on Tuesday, Singh described terrorism as one of the gravest threats to peace, development and economic prosperity. Singh said terrorism undermines not only human lives but also economic activity and social development, disrupting investment and commerce whilst depriving young people of opportunities. The Defence Minister emphasised that there can be no justification for terrorism, stating that there should be no double standards in dealing with the threat and no place for those who finance, support or provide safe havens to terrorists. His remarks came in the presence of Pakistan Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar at the regional summit. The minister stressed that the entire ecosystem of terrorism must be firmly and collectively dismantled by member states. Singh also recalled Prime Minister Narendra Modi's emphasis at the SCO Summit in Bishkek in August-September 2026 on taking concrete steps in security, connectivity and economic cooperation. He said terrorism not only claims innocent lives but also radicalises societies and deprives youth of the opportunities they rightfully deserve. While addressing connectivity and economic cooperation, Singh emphasised that connectivity projects must be based on consultation and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all countries. He stressed that projects not founded on these principles would not be sustainable, calling for simplified customs procedures, digital documentation, improved logistics and interoperable digital solutions to reduce the cost of doing business amongst SCO member states.
